description:
SUSPECTED DEFECT, UNCONFIRMED. Filed as a TODO at the maintainer's request 2026-08-05. Do not act on it as if confirmed, and do not 'fix' the sign on the strength of this bead alone.

THE OBSERVATION: PoissonRatioModel::MatproZircaloy computes nu = E/(2G) - 1 from MATPRO's independently-fitted Young's and shear modulus lines. The resulting nu INCREASES with temperature -- measured 0.386353680 at 600 K, 0.5674999999999999 at 1500 K, crossing the incompressible limit 0.5 at 1354.84 K (this crossing is what op-6sl.7 gates on, now refused rather than clamped in LinearElastic::from_models).

WHY THAT LOOKS WRONG: the abstract of Northwood (1975) on Zircaloy elastic constants states that measured Poisson's ratio DECREASES with temperature. If that is right, the port reproduces a correlation whose temperature derivative has the opposite sign to the measurement it is meant to represent -- and the 0.5 crossover would be an artefact of the sign error rather than a real (if unguarded) upstream defect.

WHY IT IS UNCONFIRMED: only the ABSTRACT was read. The paper itself is unread because outbound egress in this container blocks every literature host (see the egress bead). An abstract is not sufficient evidence to overturn a transcription -- it does not say over what temperature range, for what alloy/texture/cold-work state, or whether the quoted trend is of measured nu or of a derived quantity.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, in order:
1. Read Northwood 1975 in full and record the actual nu(T) table with its range and material condition.
2. Re-derive nu = E/(2G) - 1 from the MATPRO E and G fits as transcribed here and check the port reproduces MATPRO's own arithmetic -- i.e. separate 'did we transcribe correctly?' from 'is MATPRO right?'. These are different questions and only the first is this port's responsibility.
3. Only if the transcription is faithful AND the literature contradicts MATPRO: document it as an upstream defect with the measurement cited, exactly as the rkdcha.F90 and nmvpir.F90 discrepancies are handled. Reproduce, pin with a test, never silently correct.

DEPENDS ON THE EGRESS BLOCKER. This cannot be resolved in this container.

Related: op-6sl.7 (crossover gating, now decided -- refuse), docs/validation/poisson_ratio_zircaloy.md (the validation case, whose benchmark data is blocked on the same egress problem).

---
RE-FILED 2026-08-12 with its original id. This bead was created in an earlier session but never published, because beads-rs `bd` could not push the store ref (kopitiam#19). It survived only in the local v1 store, which diverged from origin's migrated v2 store. Preserved at ref refs/beads/local-preserve-20260812. Original status at preservation: open.
title: materials: MATPRO Zircaloy dnu/dT may have the WRONG SIGN -- literature unread, egress blocked

description:
The code-to-code sweep (op-b4a.2.5) found two inputs where upstream TRISO-ATOPS de374c8 raises instead of returning. Both are pinned by tests in tests/triso_atops_code_to_code.rs and documented in docs/triso-atops-code-to-code.md; neither has been reported upstream.

1. RB_fail_Noble_Gases raises UnboundLocalError for He/Ne/Ar/Rn (Z in {2,10,18,86}). Its if/elif chain covers z==36 and (z==54 or z in halogens) with no else, so the result is never bound -- yet these are genuine noble gases the correlation nominally covers. The Rust port is total and applies the Xe fit.

2. clean_up has no 'beta - lam == 0' guard, though its sibling plate_out does. k_plate == k_clean == 0 therefore raises ZeroDivisionError upstream; the port reproduces the missing guard and yields NaN from 0.0/0.0. Latent, not live: higher_activities only calls clean_up when a clean-up system exists (k_clean > 0).

Deliverable is a GitHub issue against IdahoLabResearch/TRISO-ATOPS, at the maintainer's discretion -- NOT a patch (workspace rule: consume upstream, do not modify it). Repo is outside this session's GitHub scope; needs add_repo first.
title: Report two upstream TRISO-ATOPS defects found by code-to-code verification

description:
Regression found 2026-09-17 during tracker reconciliation, introduced by commit bc5516ad0617 ("mc+njoy: work the four open items -- price ANGLE_TOL, land 8 tally filters, couple depletion to transport, and exclude both op-os8x leads"), which changed outram-mc-libs' Tally.filters from Vec<Box<dyn Filter>> to Vec<FilterKind> (per op-mb59 / op-6tz.36, enum dispatch over trait objects) but did not update outram-blender, its only other in-workspace consumer.

REPRODUCE:
  cargo check -p outram-blender --lib --features mc-export

  error[E0308]: mismatched types
   --> crates/outram-blender/src/sim.rs:334:23
    |
334 |         filters: vec![filter],
    |                       ^^^^^^ expected `FilterKind`, found `Box<dyn Filter>`

crates/outram-blender/src/sim.rs:330 constructs `let filter: Box<dyn Filter> = Box::new(CellFilter { cell_indices });` and pushes it into a Tally, whose filters field is now `Vec<FilterKind>` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/tally/tally.rs:80).

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT: mc-export is NOT a default Cargo feature on outram-blender (see crates/outram-blender/Cargo.toml), so `cargo check -p outram-blender --lib` (no --all-targets, no --features) is clean. It only surfaces with --features mc-export, which is presumably not part of the default workspace-wide `cargo check --workspace --lib --tests` sweep either since it's an optional feature, not a default one -- worth checking whether CI/local checks actually exercise this feature.

FIX: change crates/outram-blender/src/sim.rs's cell_flux_tally to build `FilterKind::Cell(CellFilter { cell_indices })` instead of `Box<dyn Filter>`. Small, one call site (grep confirms exactly one Box<dyn Filter> left in the workspace, at sim.rs:330). Also brings outram-blender's own filter construction into line with the workspace's no-trait-objects rule, which the outram-mc-libs side already enforces.

Related: op-mb59, op-6tz.36 (the enum-dispatch asks this refactor satisfies on the outram-mc-libs side).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
CONFIRMED FIXED 2026-09-17. The one-line fix in crates/outram-blender/src/sim.rs (FilterKind::Cell(CellFilter{..}) replacing Box<dyn Filter>) was already in the working tree when this session started; verified clean across every feature/target combo:
  cargo check -p outram-blender --lib --features mc-export
  cargo check -p outram-blender --all-targets --features mc-export
  cargo check -p outram-blender --all-targets --features foam-mesh
  cargo check -p outram-blender --all-targets --all-features
  cargo check -p outram-blender --all-targets   (default, no features)
All clean, 0 errors. Workspace-wide grep confirms zero remaining Box<dyn Filter> sites outside outram-mc-libs' own doc comments/tests. NOTE (maintainer scope change, same session): outram-blender's mc-export bridge may move into nee_soon as an ungated example -- no restructuring done here per that instruction, only the compile verification this bead asked for.

Sweep for siblings (workspace CLAUDE.md class of bug -- API moved, non-default target/feature not in the standard check) also found and fixed an UNRELATED instance of the same root problem in a different crate: crates/boon-lay's three egui example apps (first_passage_realtime.rs, triso_simulator/triso_simulator_v1/mod.rs, boon_lay_decay_simulator/decay_simulator_v1/mod.rs) still called the pre-eframe-0.34-migration egui::TopBottomPanel/SidePanel API (.show(&ctx, ..)) while the rest of the workspace had already migrated to the unified egui::Panel::{top,left,right,bottom}(..).show(ui, ..) plus .min_size() (renamed from .min_width()). Fixed the same way as the rest of the workspace (mechanical rename, no behaviour change). cargo check -p boon-lay --all-targets now clean. Filed separately if warranted -- see hand-off.

description: GH issue #35 checkpoint S17. Confirmed real gap in pdf_reader.rs's ViewMode design (op-9vo6.11): annotate_page is its own independent field from the embedded PdfReader's internal current_page(), and nothing syncs annotate_page = reader.current_page() when the operator switches Read -> Annotate mid-session -- so a reader on page 87 in Read mode drops back to whatever annotate_page last was (0, on first switch) the moment Annotate is selected. Fix: sync annotate_page from reader.current_page() at the point mode flips Read -> Annotate (the one direction that's actually achievable -- see the module doc's own 'Known gap' note on why the reverse, Annotate -> Read, has no public API to do the same; that direction stays out of scope pending kopitiam#105). Also preserve zoom across the switch (currently a single self.zoom field already IS shared, so likely already correct -- verify with a test, don't assume).
title: PDF Reader: switching Read/Annotate/Crop resets to page 1 instead of preserving page+zoom+viewport
